podcast.body: Bob Lannwaw, David Botrell's mentor, worked on this U2 album, which was part of his work before Peter Gabriel called him for the *Birdy* soundtrack. "he went over to do the unforgettable fire and then came with you too and then came back"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released in 1984, this album represented another significant leap forward for U2, making their sound more sophisticated, stronger, bigger, and better. Produced by Brian Eno and Daniel Landwom, it introduced new textures and sonics that were markedly different from previous U2 work, including songs like "Bad" and "The Name of Love." Initial recording took place at Slane Castle. "That represented another leap forward. Things seemed more sophisticated, stronger, bigger, better."
